title: LLM2SVG: looking closely at SVG data

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ask an AI for a vector drawing and you get SVG code. But is that code actually valid, and what does good SVG look like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's what this project looks into?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. This LLM2SVG fork gathers SVG dataset utilities and an evaluation-oriented scaffold. It's a place to inspect examples and understand the constraints of the format.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The project describes a structured prompt framework plus a Python validator, aimed at getting crisp, valid SVG illustrations out of language model answers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I like that way of putting it. It's all Python, a small codebase, with the upstream project credited.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Handy if you want to understand SVG data before building on it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The written page walks through it.
